title: NALCO Q1 Profit Jumps 91% to ₹2,003 Crore on Surging Aluminium Prices
excerpt: India's state-owned aluminium producer posts its strongest quarterly profit since FY26's record year, driven by higher metal realizations and expanded production volumes.
body:
• NALCO's Q1 FY27 net profit surged 90.8% year-on-year to ₹2,003 crore, up from ₹1,049 crore in Q1 FY26.
  • Revenue from operations rose to approximately ₹5,300 crore, a 39% increase over the year-ago quarter's ₹3,807 crore.
  • Aluminium prices have been supported by supply disruptions linked to the Middle East conflict and reduced Chinese smelter output.
  • NALCO signed a joint venture with NLC India in July to build a 1,080 MW captive power plant in Odisha for its smelter expansion.

Record-Setting Quarter

National Aluminium Company (NALCO) reported first-quarter net profit of ₹2,003 crore for the three months ended June 30, 2026, nearly doubling from ₹1,049 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations climbed to approximately ₹5,300 crore, according to results approved by the company's board of directors on Thursday.

The results mark NALCO's strongest quarterly performance relative to Q1 comparisons and build on the momentum of FY26, when the Bhubaneswar-based company posted record full-year net profit of ₹5,816 crore on revenue of ₹17,843 crore.

Aluminium Prices Underpin the Surge

The sharp profit jump was driven primarily by higher aluminium realizations. The benchmark three-month aluminium price on the London Metal Exchange has remained elevated through the June quarter, supported by several overlapping factors: reduced Chinese smelter output due to environmental restrictions and winter power curtailments, lower global inventories and supply-chain disruptions stemming from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

NALCO's aluminium business — which accounts for more than half of total revenue — has been the primary beneficiary. The company produces aluminium at its integrated complex in Odisha, where captive bauxite mining and power generation provide a cost advantage over competitors reliant on external inputs.

Production Expansion on Track

NALCO has been steadily scaling production across its value chain. In FY26, the company recorded its highest-ever output for alumina hydrate (23 lakh tonnes), calcined alumina (22.75 lakh tonnes) and cast metal (4.72 lakh tonnes). Bauxite excavation reached 77.01 lakh tonnes, while captive coal production hit 40 lakh tonnes.

The company is targeting coal production of 4.8 million tonnes in FY27 to cover a larger share of its power requirements, a move designed to insulate its cost base from volatile energy markets. Progress on the Pottangi bauxite mines and a fifth-stream alumina refinery expansion remain key projects to watch.

"The company's strong results were driven by a combination of cost-efficient operations, a favourable domestic business climate, and significant increase in volumes."

— Brijendra Pratap Singh, Chairman & Managing Director, NALCO

Strategic Partnerships for Growth

On July 8, NALCO signed a joint venture agreement with NLC India Limited to build a 1,080 MW coal-based captive power plant in Angul, Odisha. The facility is designed to provide stable, lower-cost electricity for NALCO's planned aluminium smelter expansion, addressing one of the most significant cost pressures facing Indian aluminium producers.

Despite the strong quarter, analysts have flagged rising input costs — caustic soda prices have climbed from around ₹42,000 to ₹45,000 per tonne, while calcined petroleum coke prices have risen to ₹50,000-53,000 per tonne. These increases could add ₹5,000-6,000 per tonne to aluminium production costs.

Outlook

Aluminium prices are expected to remain supported in the near term by continued supply disruptions, though NALCO's management has cautioned that alumina prices could face downward pressure. EBITDA margins may soften slightly from FY26's elevated levels due to higher depreciation linked to expansion projects and rising raw material costs. Rival Vedanta reported a 92.3% rise in Q4 FY26 profit, while Hindalco's results are still pending.
